notes:
Summary: enterprise procurement for dedicated GPU pools + private control plane. Primary ask is firm throughput guarantees and a clear SLA credit schedule. Team: CTO (James Kwan), Head of ML Infra (Elena Ruiz), Cloud SRE lead (Markus Hsu). AE Evan Morales; SE Priya Raman; CSM Liam O'Connor.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-21: Intro call (AE intro). High level requirements captured: low-latency chat (p50 < 40ms), p99 < 250ms for 8k context flow, steady-state throughput target 8k tokens/sec across pool.
- 2026-02-03: Technical deep-dive with SREs + model engineers. Ran baseline QPS test; Redwood dedicated suggestion: 8x A100-equivalent reserved with 20% burst pool. Notes in drive. (ff_2026-02-08_8392ab).
- 2026-02-15: Security questionnaire submitted; require SOC2 type II + KMS integration and audit logs retention 3 years.
- 2026-02-22: POC scoping meeting. Agreed on 30-day POC with synthetic load and customer traffic shadowing; target POC SLOs: 99.95% uptime, median latency p50 < 45ms, p99 < 300ms under 75% load.
- 2026-03-01: Contract framework call with procurement. Customer pushed for 99.99% uptime and 5x credits for downtime. Redwood proposed 99.95% uptime, tiered credit schedule (see credit schedule below).

Key technical requirements / asks:
- Throughput: guaranteed baseline tokens/sec and concurrency slots; expectation for scaling within 60s to burst capacity for traffic spikes.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms under committed baseline.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial commit 8 GPU-equivalents (A100-class), ability to increase within 30 days with price adjust; dedicated pool must be isolated per legal team.
- Routing/fallback: requirement for automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant with no more than 2x p99 latency during overload.
- Maintenance windows: customer requests maintenance blackout 08:00-20:00 local for trading hours (M-F). Redwood proposes one 2-hour weekly window and one monthly 4-hour window outside blackout in exchange for compensation credits if outside-window maintenance occurs.
- Support response times: P1 30m initial response, P2 2 hours, P3 1 business day; 24/7 on-call for severity P1.
- Data controls: KMS for key management, customer-managed VPC, audit logs forwarded to customer's SIEM, data residency (NA-only).

SLA / credit schedule (current proposal):
- Uptime >=99.95%: no credits.
- Uptime 99.90% - 99.94%: 10% monthly service credit.
- Uptime 99.00% - 99.89%: 30% monthly service credit.
- Uptime <99.00%: 50% monthly service credit plus option to terminate with pro-rata refund.
- Emergency maintenance (unscheduled) that impacts >10% of reserved capacity: 2x credit multiplier for that incident.
- Credits capped at 100% of monthly committed fee.

Open negotiation points / customer pushbacks:
- Customer insists on 99.99% uptime for trading-critical flows; legal wants a narrower credit ladder and SLA termination triggers.
- Procurement wants guaranteed CPU/GPU affinity (no noisy neighbors) for dedicated nodes; Redwood to confirm isolation model.
- Maintenance blackout: customer demands no maintenance during trading hours; Redwood asks for limited exceptions with compensation.
- Support SLAs: customer wants guaranteed on-site engineering support for 2 weeks after go-live for cutover; Redwood suggested dedicated onboarding package at additional cost.

POC plan and success metrics:
- 30-day POC using mixed production shadow traffic + synthetic spike tests.
- Success criteria: meet p50/p99 SLOs for 28/30 days, demonstrate autoscaling within 60s to 2x baseline for 90% of spike events, verify audit log delivery and KMS integration, complete security checklist.

Next steps (short):
- Draft redline of SLA by Redwood legal (Evan to deliver by 2026-03-12).
- Joint legal call week of 2026-03-15 to resolve uptime % and credit caps.
- Prepare POC runbook and credentials; SE Priya to share runbook by 2026-03-10.

Notes / quotes from customer:
- "We need predictability — if we lose a trading window we lose tens of millions." — CTO James Kwan.
- "Maintenance can't be during market hours; that is non-negotiable without a hard credit schedule." — Head of SRE Markus Hsu.

Internal red flags:
- High ARR expectations but aggressive SLA demands may require higher engineering commitment and potential pricing adjustment.
- Legal likely to push for termination rights that Redwood should limit to catastrophic failures only.
